article_text:
Once Upon a Time in Harlem is continuing its strong push for Oscar recognition, earning five nominations Tuesday for the Critics Choice Documentary Awards. That’s added to the distinction of premiering at Sundance, and being honored with berths at the Cannes, Telluride, Toronto and New York film festivals – the only documentary to do so this year.

The film directed by David Greaves and produced by Liani Greaves (David’s daughter) is based on extraordinary footage from an event in 1972 – a reunion for one afternoon only of the surviving members of the Harlem Renaissance. They gathered at the home of Duke Ellington for what would be a final opportunity to renew friendships, share stories and engage in vigorous debate about the Harlem Renaissance, its artists and scholars, and Black cultural and political life in America.

Watch on Deadline

The documentary, based on material shot by William Greaves – David’s father and Liani’s grandfather – opens theatrically in New York this Friday and in Los Angeles on October 23. David and Liani join the latest edition of Deadline’s Doc Talk podcast to discuss their remarkable nonfiction feature and how they crafted it from almost 30 hours of raw footage.

David was one of the original cameramen on the 1972 shoot. He recalls working with his father to capture the once-in-a-lifetime gathering and how William wanted the finished film “to be a theatrical experience that moves at a snappy pace.” Liani reflects on her grandfather who was a true Renaissance man himself: actor, sculptor, poet, dancer, songwriter and filmmaker.

RELATED: ‘Once Upon A Time In Harlem’ Trailer: Oscar Contender Reveals Extraordinary Reunion Of Harlem Renaissance Leaders

The Greaves also explore the interpersonal dynamics at play in the reunion of so many artists and thinkers who gathered that day in Harlem. Disagreements emerged among the group on how to define the Harlem Renaissance and whether its legacy would continue or be lost. The Greaves speak to the importance of women to the Harlem Renaissance and how their integral role is sometimes overlooked.

Certain frictions or frustrations became apparent during the reunion as some of those women tried to make their voices heard in the din of lively conversation.

Liani Greaves reveals why the presence of George Schuyler at the gathering triggered strong emotions among some of the attendees (having to do with his contrarian politics). She also relates one unflattering remark aimed at Schuyler — a moment not included in the documentary. Doc Talk co-host John Ridley explains why he particularly identified with comments made in the film by Richard Bruce Nugent, one of those fascinating living luminaries of the Harlem Renaissance featured in the documentary.

That’s on the new episode of Doc Talk hosted by Oscar winner Ridley ( 12 Years a Slave , Shirley ) and Matt Carey, Deadline’s senior documentary editor. The pod is a production of Deadline and Ridley’s Nō Studios.

Listen to the episode above or on major podcast platforms including Spotify , iHeart and Apple .

article_text:
Der niederländische Kunsthistoriker, Kurator und Museumsdirektor Rudi Fuchs ist im Alter von 84 Jahren gestorben

Wie seine Familie am Montag bekannt gab, verstarb er am Sonntagabend in Amsterdam. Geboren 1942 in Eindhoven, prägte Rudi Fuchs über fast drei Jahrzehnte hinweg bedeutende Institutionen: Er leitete das Van Abbemuseum in Eindhoven, das Gemeentemuseum in Den Haag und von 1993 bis 2003 das Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam. International wirkte er zudem als erster Direktor des Castello di Rivoli bei Turin sowie als künstlerischer Leiter der Documenta 7 in Kassel im Jahr 1982.

Neben seiner kuratorischen Arbeit war Fuchs ein vielseitiger Publizist. Zwischen 2009 und 2022 schrieb er wöchentlich über Kunst für "De Groene Amsterdammer" und veröffentlichte unter anderem Bücher über Karel Appel und Rembrandt.

article_text:
美術館連絡協議会（美連協）は、 47 都道府県の美術館約 150 館が加盟する団体です。全国の美術館が連携を図り、芸術、文化の向上および発展に資することを目的にしています。

【美術人ナビ】では、美連協加盟館の推進力となっている美術人のインタビューを毎回お届けします。第５弾は、 2022 年から約 4 年間にわたる大規模改修を経て、 2026 年にリニューアルオープンした江戸東京博物館・事業企画課長の新田太郎さんに聞きました。

東京都江戸東京博物館

所在地：東京都墨田区横網 1-4-1

休館日：月曜日（祝日・振替休日の場合は翌日）、年末年始

開館時間： 9:30 ～ 17:30 （土曜日は 19:30 まで。入館は閉館 30 分前まで）

観覧料：常設展（企画展を含む）一般 800 円、 65 歳以上 400 円、大学生・専門学校生 480 円、高校生 300 円、中学生以下無料。特別展は別料金。

公式 HP ： https://www.edo-tokyo-museum.or.jp/

原寸大の日本橋や江戸の町並みを再現した江戸東京博物館の巨大な展示空間は、 1993 年の開館以来、多くの人を魅了してきました。そこでインタビュー前半では、同館の設立経緯や 30 年以上にわたる歩み、展示に込められた思いについて伺いました。

東京の人々に「共通の歴史」を――江戸博誕生と「江戸東京学」

―― まずは江戸東京博物館が生まれた経緯を教えてください。

新田 当館の設立の経緯は、『江戸東京博物館建設のあゆみ―建設と開設準備のあゆみ』（東京都歴史文化財団 1997年）などの報告書にまとめられています。それによると、構想が具体化したのは鈴木俊一都知事の在任時に構想された「マイタウン東京」の検討が始まった1980年からです。東京には進学や仕事のために他の地域から移り住んだ人が大勢います。そういう方々にも、自分が暮らす街に愛着を持ってもらいたい。そのためには、東京の成り立ちや人々が共有できる歴史を知ることが大切だ、という考え方のもと、東京の文化的なシンボルとなる施設の一つとして江戸東京博物館が構想されました。設置場所が両国になったのは、東京都庁が有楽町から西寄りの新宿へ移るなか、東京東部の自治体などから文化施設を置きたいという要望があり、その中から、まとまった用地があり、交通が便利で、江戸東京の歴史とのゆかりが深いこの地が選ばれたそうです。

―― なぜ「東京都博物館」ではなく「江戸東京博物館」と名付けられたのでしょうか。

新田 「マイタウン東京」が構想されるごく初期の段階から「江戸・東京の文化を保存し、次代に継承する」ことが謳われていました。歴史を振り返ると、現在の東京という都市のルーツは徳川家康が関東に入府した 1590 年まで遡ることができるからです。家康は江戸城を中心とする城下町の整備を進めて、利根川や荒川の治水事業や堀の整備といった大規模な土木事業を行い、現在の東京につながる都市の骨格を形作りました。つまり、江戸時代は今の東京という都市の出発点として考えることができます。そこで、江戸と東京を別々のものとして捉えるのではなく、 400 年以上にわたる一つの都市の歴史として研究し、紹介していこうということになり、館名にも「江戸」というキーワードが入ったようです。その学術的な基盤となったのが「江戸東京学」です。

―― 「江戸東京学」とはどのような学問なのでしょうか？

新田 歴史学だけでなく、美術、文学、考古、民俗、建築、地理、政治、経済など、さまざまな分野の研究者が協力し、江戸から東京に至る都市の形成や文化の変化を、多角的に捉えようとする学際的な試みでした。理論的な支柱となった小木新造先生は、いわば「生活者の歴史学」を重視されました。偉い人や大きな事件の歴史だけではなく、普通の人々がどこで、どのように暮らしてきたのかに目を向ける。江戸時代と明治以降をきっぱり分けるのではなく、暮らしの中にある連続性と変化の両方を見ようということです。例えば明治維新を境に食生活が一変したわけではありません。人の生活はもっと緩やかに変わっていく。この「江戸東京学」の成果が展示へと色濃く反映されているのが、江戸博の大きな特徴となっています。

「ガラクタ」にも歴史がある――35万点の資料と巨大な復元展示

―― その理念は、展示や資料の集め方にどのように反映されているのでしょうか。

新田 初代の児玉幸多館長から、小木新三館長、竹内誠館長、そして現在の藤森照信館長の指導のもと、われわれ学芸員が収集活動で重視してきたのは、市井の人々の暮らしを支えてきた身近な品々です。例えば、戦時中の疎開児童が使ったアルマイトの弁当箱や、かつて汲み取り式トイレで使われていた桶やひしゃくなど。一般には「ガラクタ」と思われるようなものもありますが、そうした品々こそ、市場に出回ることがほとんどなく、購入しようにも手に入りません。そもそも日用品は使い古されれば捨てられ、着物なども最後はほどいて雑巾にするなど、使い尽くされてしまうため、意外なほど残っていないんです。収集には美術品や由緒ある名品とは異なる難しさがありますが、都民の皆様に働きかけて寄贈していただくなど、一点一点、地道に集めてきました。

―― 現在はどのくらいの資料を所蔵しているのですか。

新田 約 35 万点です。別に図書も約 29 万冊所蔵しています。展示をきっかけに、「うちにも同じようなものがあります」とご連絡いただき、寄贈につながることもあります。捨てられてしまいそうだったものに歴史資料としての価値があると、気づいていただけるんですね。

―― 開館当初から、日本橋や町並みの実物大模型は大きな話題になりました。

新田 博物館というと珍しいものがケースに並んでいる印象があるかもしれませんね。ですが、幅広い分野の数多くの有識者による検討を経て、約 9000 平方メートルという大空間を活かし、展示物そのものの中に入っていけるような展示空間が作られました。常設展示室に入ると、まず日本橋が現れる。それも橋を上から眺めるのではなく、自分でその上に立つことができる。江戸時代に一瞬タイムスリップしたような、非日常的な体験が味わえます。精巧なジオラマも好評を博しました。

―― 著名な建築家である菊竹清訓さんが手掛けた高床式の建物も独特ですね。

新田 江戸博のある両国は、東京東部の下町低地にあたります。そのため、水害への備えとして、常設展示室や収蔵庫を高い位置に配置する設計が採用されました。構造としては、巨大な橋の上に屋根と壁を載せたようなものです。一方、建物を持ち上げることで、その下には広大な空間が生まれます。菊竹さんは、そこを人々が自由に行き交い、交流できる広場にしようと考えたのです。それが「江戸東京ひろば」で、現在もさまざまな用途に活用しています。東京の中心部に近い場所で、これほど広々とした開放的な空間は、なかなか珍しいのではないでしょうか。

「ポンペイ展」が大きな転機に――特別展に見る30年の歩み

―― 開館後の特別展を振り返ると、どんな変化がありましたか。

新田 1993 年の第 1 回特別展は「家康の遺産 駿府御分物展」でした。家康の残した遺産に光を当てた、まさに江戸幕府の始まりを示す展覧会です。むしろ江戸博らしかったのは、続く第 2 回の「博覧都市 江戸東京展」かもしれません。江戸の寺社での開帳や縁日、盛り場から近代の博覧会へと、人が集い、楽しむ都市の文化をたどるものです。江戸が祝祭的な都市だったことを示した展覧会でした。

―― その後は海外の歴史文化を扱う展覧会も開催されるようになります。

新田 開館した年は約 300 万人が来館しましたが、その後、入館者数は減っていきました。そこで自主企画だけでなく、メディアと組んだ展覧会などにも取り組むようになりました。印象深かったのが、特別展「世界遺産 ポンペイ展 古代ローマの輝き」（ 2001 年 8 月 7 日～ 10 月 28 日）です。多彩な出土資料により、都市の記憶がまざまざと目の前に現れる展示は評判を得て、、約 2 ヶ月半の会期中、過去最高となる約 38 万人にご来場いただくことができました。江戸博の特別展のカラーが変わる転機になったと思います。

―― 現在、特別展と企画展には、それぞれどんな役割があるのでしょうか。

新田 特別展には、これまで江戸博に関心がなかった人にも足を運んでもらう、いわば「広告塔」としての役割があります。リニューアル開館第一弾として開催した特別展「大江戸礼賛」では、館蔵コレクションから選りすぐった名品を集めることで、改装前からのリピーターの方はもちろん、初めて江戸博にいらっしゃる方にも当館がどのような博物館なのか、その特徴をお示しすることができたと思います。

――では、企画展はどのような狙いをもって開催されているのでしょうか？

新田 一方、常設展料金で入場できる企画展では、常設展示だけでは十分に紹介できない資料や、集客という点では難しくても、当館として取り組むべきテーマを扱っています。全国各地の発掘調査の最新成果を紹介する「新発見考古速報 発掘された日本列島」展や都民の皆様からご寄贈いただいた新規収蔵資料を出品する「市民からのおくりもの」など、毎年継続して紹介したいテーマもあります。大勢の方に来てもらうことと、歴史を掘り下げ、残していくこと。今後も、展覧会の企画を立てる際は、その両方の狙いをバランスよく追求していきたいと考えています。（後編へ続く、聞き手、ライター・齋藤久嗣）

article_text:
Debutterà il 21 novembre 2026 Rubaiya Qatar , la nuova quadriennale internazionale di arte contemporanea promossa da Qatar Museums , che fino al 30 aprile 2027 coinvolgerà musei, spazi espositivi e luoghi pubblici di Doha. La prima edizione riunirà oltre 120 artisti provenienti da più di 45 Paesi, con oltre 45 nuove commissioni, sviluppando un programma incentrato sull’ecologia globale, sul ruolo dell’acqua nella storia dell’umanità e sul patrimonio marittimo del Qatar e della regione del Golfo.

Istituita sotto la guida di Sheikha Al Mayassa bint Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani , presidente di Qatar Museums, la manifestazione è organizzata da ALRIWAQ Arts + Architecture e si diffonderà tra la sede recentemente rinnovata dell’istituzione, il Museum of Islamic Art, la Katara QM Gallery, il Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art e diversi spazi pubblici del Paese.

Già con la sua prima edizione, Rubaiya Qatar vuole entrare nel sistema delle grandi manifestazioni periodiche internazionali scegliendo un tema fortemente radicato nella geografia del Golfo ma sviluppato su scala globale. Acqua, rotte marittime, crisi ambientale e circolazione di persone e idee diventano i vettori di una manifestazione che punta a collocare Doha come una delle capitali nella geografia culturale dell’area SWANA.

L’acqua come chiave per leggere la globalizzazione: gli artisti di Rubaiya Qatar

Cuore della quadriennale sarà Unruly Waters , mostra principale ospitata da ALRIWAQ Arts + Architecture, con ulteriori interventi al Museum of Islamic Art e nel MIA Park. Curata da Tom Eccles, Ruba Katrib, Shabbir Hussain Mustafa e Mark Rappolt , l’esposizione prende il titolo dall’omonimo libro dello storico Sunil Amrith e utilizza l’acqua come strumento per rileggere la storia delle relazioni globali.

Alisei, monsoni, correnti oceaniche e rotte commerciali diventano così dispositivi attraverso cui osservare gli scambi tra culture, mettendo in relazione antiche reti marittime e sistemi contemporanei di comunicazione. Il Golfo viene interpretato non come territorio periferico o isolato, ma come crocevia storico di persone, merci, conoscenze e forme culturali.

La mostra comprenderà oltre 30 nuove commissioni. Tra gli autori coinvolti figurano Bani Abidi , Lawrence Abu Hamdan, Sophia Al-Maria, Majid Al-Remaihi, Mohamed Bourouissa, Ade Darmawan, Alia Farid, Ayoung Kim, Charles Lim, Naeem Mohaiemen, Yuko Mohri, Oscar Murillo, Priya Sen e Marina Tabassum . Il percorso sarà scandito da media e linguaggi diversi, dal cinema alla pittura, dalla scultura alla performance, fino alla cultura del cibo e alle installazioni digitali sviluppate anche attraverso l’intelligenza artificiale.

Accanto alle opere contemporanee saranno inoltre presentati reperti provenienti dal relitto della nave di Cirebon, risalente al X secolo e rinvenuto al largo di Giava. Conservati nelle collezioni di Qatar Museums, questi materiali saranno messi in relazione con opere del Museum of Islamic Art e nuove commissioni, ricostruendo la densità degli scambi sviluppatisi lungo la Via della Seta marittima.

Rubaiya Qatar: 12 artisti per Our Common Currents

Dal 22 novembre, alla QM Katara Gallery, aprirà Our Common Currents , curata da Lina Patmali . La mostra prosegue la riflessione sull’acqua spostando l’attenzione sulla relazione quotidiana tra esseri umani e ambiente, dal valore rituale e simbolico dell’elemento alle sue funzioni nell’agricoltura, nell’industria e nelle attività ricreative.

12 artisti internazionali affronteranno temi come mari, laghi, fiumi, iceberg, maree, aridità, pesca, nuoto e desalinizzazione. Quattro saranno le nuove commissioni, affiancate da prestiti provenienti, tra gli altri, dalla collezione del futuro Art Mill Museum.

Tra i nuovi lavori figura un’installazione scultorea site specific di Taloi Havini , accompagnata da un giardino con piante autoctone del deserto e mangrovie; un intervento ambientale di Latent Community dedicato ai paesaggi di transizione tra deserto e mare; un video di Miguel Fernández de Castro che mette in relazione il cavallo arabo, la desalinizzazione e il sale; un’installazione digitale e tessile di Artcom Platform ispirata al lago Balkhash e alle comunità che ne abitano le sponde.

Il Golfo e il mare al Mathaf

Un terzo nucleo sarà costituito da Seething Sea , in programma dal 22 novembre al Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art. Curata da Wadha Al-Aqeedi , con Loulwah Kutbi come assistant curator, la mostra prende il titolo da un’immagine del mare contenuta nel Corano e concentra lo sguardo sulla relazione millenaria tra le comunità del Golfo e le sue acque.

Fede, folklore, rituali e artigianato vengono riletti alla luce delle trasformazioni contemporanee legate allo sfruttamento delle risorse, al degrado ambientale e ai conflitti. Il percorso si articolerà attorno alla creazione, alla vita sostenuta dal mare e all’incontro tra una prospettiva apocalittica religiosa e quella ecologica. Saranno presentati oltre 50 artisti e più di 80 lavori provenienti dalla collezione del Mathaf e da prestiti, insieme a una nuova installazione monumentale commissionata a Jasem AlSanea.

Nuove opere nello spazio pubblico

Rubaiya Qatar uscirà inoltre dagli spazi museali con una serie di interventi permanenti o temporanei distribuiti in diverse aree del Paese.

Al MIA Park tornerà untitled 2025 (no bread no ashes) di Rirkrit Tiravanija , concepita come luogo di incontro e condivisione di cibo e idee. Jitish Kallat presenterà invece Here After Here After Here 25°17′33″N 51°32′46″E , una scultura circolare ispirata alla forma della segnaletica stradale.

Sono inoltre previsti un intervento di Ibrahim Mahama destinato al futuro Art Mill Museum, un lavoro di Lubna Chowdhary alle Torri di Barzan, un murale di Minerva Cuevas nella stazione della metropolitana del National Museum of Qatar, un’area gioco progettata da Shaikha Hala Al Khalifa ad Al Khor e una scultura di Nazgol Ansarinia nella piazza Al Qubaib.

Cinque mesi di incontri, performance e workshop

La quadriennale sarà accompagnata per tutta la sua durata da un programma pubblico che coinvolgerà oltre 130 artisti, curatori, ricercatori, educatori e professionisti della cultura. Incontri con gli artisti, conferenze, performance, workshop, proiezioni e visite guidate saranno distribuiti in diversi luoghi del Qatar, insieme a collaborazioni con istituzioni accademiche e iniziative rivolte alle comunità locali.

article_text:
For the past five years, Stephan Vanfleteren (1969), an internationally renowned photographer, has maintained an almost obsessive relationship with the sea. A profound fascination at once compelling and dangerous has led him to explore this ever-changing, elusive and unpredictable world. With *Transcripts of a Sea* , he offers a personal interpretation of the sea, captured in all its diversity, through its moods, movements and shifting light.

Whether stormy or as calm as a mirror, shrouded in mist, swept by a storm, deceptively peaceful or churning like the drum of a washing machine, the sea is constantly transforming before his eyes. But Stephan Vanfleteren does not observe it from the shore or from the deck of a boat. He chooses direct, physical and sensory engagement: he literally steps into the water, immerses himself in this element and allows himself to be carried along by its power.

First presented to the public in September 2025 at the Museum of Fine Arts in Ghent (MSK), Transcripts of a Sea was an immediate and remarkable success, attracting over 140,000 visitors. Since then, the exhibition has continued its international tour. It is currently on display at the Maritime Museum in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, where it will remain open until April 2027.

Perhaps we should leave the appreciation to an expert:

(Stephan Vanfleteren is) A navigator without a boat, Stephan Vanfleteren seems to have adopted the castaway’s point of view. His body, held upright according to a performative protocol, finds its origins in a childhood memory: an accident involving near-drowning, whose outcome was ultimately a fortunate one. A rescue, like a second birth, that must be relived… Between each image, one must draw breath anew.

Do not look for the line of horizon. What you perceive is, more often than not, a waterline.

The horizon itself has been cast into invisibility. All that matters now is the supple blade of a receding swell, the splash of an exhausted wave at the height of its flight, the black liquor of nocturnal water. These formless substances are not landscapes. In Transcripts of a Sea, the figure of the castaway is one and the same as the element in which he is immersed, with which he has become indivisible.

…

Transcripts of a Sea is the outcome of an experience of being alive: of imagining oneself alive in the very place where one has felt one’s own death. Above all, it is the living that draws the great category of the “elements” (water, earth, fire) out of the metaphysical realm and inscribes it within an ecological sensibility. At first glance, the universality of these “transcriptions” asserts itself like a rising tide. Transcripts of a Sea is an immense recording, measuring the pulse of life as it composes with the contours of the water and the operator’s blood pressure. The sea thus becomes a place for meditating on freedom, expressed through the choice to place oneself in danger.

Michel Poivert Professor of the History of Photography

TRANSCRIPTS OF A SEA – art book – edition of Hannibal Books

And again we present the impressive art book.

The cover is based on the notebooks he uses trip after trip to entrust his notes to. When you pick up the book, you think you are holding an oversized Leuchtturm or Moleskine, with a hard cover, rounded corners, dog-eared, water-stained, faded… and somewhere a date, a date that Stephan Vanfleteren will never forget. The cover is like a palimpsest, with layers shining through.

The book contains 136 photographs by Stephan Vanfleteren, showing the sea in all its colours and overwhelming power. Highly recommended for all lovers of the sea…

Transcripts of a Sea is available in English, French or Dutch – €79.95 Free shipping to Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg. Signed copies available through the editor at https://hannibalbooks.be/en/transcripts-of-a-sea#108736

Escrito por Simon Kinberg, nova trilogia é especulada como o próximo capítulo na Saga Skywalker.

Os Skywalker estão de volta. Segundo o THR , Jon Watts vai dirigir um novo filme de “ Star Wars “, que será o primeiro de uma nova trilogia.

O cineasta Simon Kinberg vem trabalhando na criação de uma nova trilogia para a Lucasfilm desde o final de 2024. Ao que tudo indica, o projeto deve servir como o próximo capítulo na chamada Saga Skywalker, que é composta pelos nove filmes entre “Star Wars: Episódio I — A Ameaça Fantasma” e “Star Wars: Episódio IX — A Ascensão Skywalker”. Rey Skywalker, a jovem Jedi interpretada por Daisy Ridley na trilogia lançada pela Disney entre 2015 e 2019, deve retornar na trilogia de Kinberg.

Para Watts, trata-se na verdade de seu segundo projeto da franquia. Em 2024, ele cocriou e dirigiu parte da série “Skeleton Crew”, que acompanha um grupo de crianças que se perde pela galáxia tão, tão distante em uma aventura à la “Os Goonies”. Watts é mais conhecido também por dirigir a trilogia principal de filmes do Homem-Aranha de Tom Holland para a Marvel, incluindo “Homem-Aranha: Sem Volta Para Casa”.

Segundo o relato, o projeto ainda está em desenvolvimento e não recebeu sinal verde da Disney, embora pareça ser o projeto mais avançado em produção pela Lucasfilm depois de “Star Wars: Starfighter”, estrelado por Ryan Gosling e dirigido por Shawn Levy. A princípio, também seguem em desenvolvimento os filmes de Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy, focado em Rey Skywalker, e o de James Mangold sobre a origem da Ordem Jedi.

“Star Wars: Starfighter” tem estreia prevista para 27 de maio de 2027, coincidindo com o aniversário de 50 anos da franquia.

青森県立美術館開館20周年／東日本大震災15年 志賀理江子 なぬもかぬも 2026年10月31日（土）–2027年3月14日（日） 青森県立美術館 https://www.aomori-museum.jp/ 開館時間：9:30–17:00（入館は16:30まで）※11/14、12/19、1/16は20:00まで（入館は19:30まで） 休館日：11/9、11/24、12/14、12/24-31、2027/1/1、1/12、1/25、2/8、2/13-25、3/8 企画担当：奥脇嵩大（青森県立美術館学芸員） 展覧会URL： https://www.aomori-museum.jp/schedule/18042/

青森県立美術館では、開館20周年と東日本大震災15年にあわせ、身体の感覚に根ざした色と光、演劇性のある写真作品で国際的に知られる宮城県在住のアーティスト・志賀理江子による過去最大規模の個展「志賀理江子 なぬもかぬも」を開催する。 志賀理江子 （1980年愛知県生まれ）は、2004年にロンドン芸術大学チェルシー・カレッジ・オブ・アート＆デザインを卒業した。2006年の展覧会参加を契機に宮城県沿岸部の松林の風景と出会い、2008年に宮城県名取市北釜地区へ移住。地域のカメラマンとして活動しながら北釜の人々のオーラル・ヒストリーを聞き取り、被災しながらも北釜の人々の参加により生まれた写真シリーズ〈螺旋海岸〉を発表したことで、大きな反響を呼んだ。以来宮城県内で活動し、現在は石巻を拠点とする。近年の主な展覧会に、グループ展「漂着」（アーティゾン美術館、東京、2025–2026）、「 第8回横浜トリエンナーレ 」（横浜美術館、神奈川、2024）、「リボーン・アートフェスティバル」（牡鹿半島各所、宮城、2021–2022）、個展「 ヒューマン・スプリング 」（東京都写真美術館、2019）、個展「ブラインド・デート」（猪熊弦一郎現代美術館、香川、2017）、グループ展「ニューフォトグラフィー」（ニューヨーク近代美術館、アメリカ、2015）、個展「 螺旋海岸 」（せんだいメディアテーク、宮城、2012–2013）などがある。2007年に写真集『Lilly』『CANARY』の仕事において第33回木村伊兵衛写真賞、2021–2023年に Tokyo Contemporary Art Award 、2025年に第1回梅原猛人類哲学賞を受賞した。

本展のタイトルにある「なぬもかぬも」は三陸沿岸部に伝わる方言で、「お手上げだ！」「深い海の底のため息」「一切合切」など、使う人や環境により意味がひらく言葉だという。この言葉を冠する本展は、志賀が震災前後から拠点とし、今に至るまで行き逢ってきた「東北」への洞察から生まれた写真や映像、テキスト、インスタレーション作品を新旧織りまぜて紹介する。2012–2013年のシリーズ〈螺旋海岸〉以降に生まれた写真や映像作品群から、志賀が架空の人物「褜男（えなお）」に託した物語とイメージからなる2025年の《なぬもかぬも》を、本展のために集まったサポートスタッフの手も借りながら再構成するほか、2022年の《あの夜のつながるところ》と2022–2023年の《風の吹くとき》を、イメージとテキストからなる本展にあわせたバージョンで紹介する。あわせて、完全新作による写真や映像作品なども展開される予定となっている。 会期中には、「東北」「エネルギー」「核」「イメージ」をテーマに、志賀の案内により、志賀に影響を与え続けるさまざまな分野の人々の言葉と実践を通して作品の源泉にふれるトークイベントなどを多数開催する。また、ミュージアムショップ内では、石巻の志賀のスタジオ「ENA」とつながりのある人々の拠点「MIMIZU」「日月羊 Works Lab.」「東北朝鮮学校とつながる宮城の会IO」「실（Sil／糸）」「Irregular Rhythm Asylum」ほかのアーティストや作り手による品々を販売する。

SPOILER ALERT : This article contains spoilers for “ Clayface ,” now playing in theaters.

Batman fans will have to wait patiently for the next installment in Matt Reeves and Robert Pattinson’s Caped Crusader saga, but they can get a peek at the rebooted DC Universe’s Gotham City in “Clayface.”

“Clayface” is an R-rated body horror that follows the shape-shifting Batman foe. It blends a supervillain origin story with some stomach-churning scares and comes from horror veterans including director James Watkins and a story by Mike Flanagan. Tom Rhys Harries plays Matt Hagen, an A-list actor who is brutally disfigured by a gangster. With his face ripped up and his career destroyed, Matt turns to an experimental procedure from Dr. Caitlyn Corr (Naomi Ackie), which heals him — but slowly turns him into a clay-covered monster.

Matt’s blood cells gain the ability to transform and instantly reshape his body into someone else, such as Corr or the gangster who disfigured him or even his own father (played in a quick cameo by Aaron Paul ). He loses control of his own body and sanity as these newfound shape-shifting powers help him enact bloody revenge on the mob who ruined his life. In the end, Matt kills everybody who wronged him (plus several innocent people), and is forced to live as a reclusive mud monster in the sewers.

Popular on Variety

Clayface has appeared in many Batman comics through the years, and he’s a classic villain who’s made the crossover into animated shows and video games. This version of him has also technically already appeared in the rebooted DC Universe in James Gunn’s animated series “Creature Commandos,” but now the monster gets his own origin story and live-action debut. The movie also gives the first look at Batman’s hometown of Gotham City in the new DC Universe. Gunn’s “Superman” kicked things off in Metropolis last year, but now another one of DC’s most famous cities gets unveiled in “Clayface.”

With Variety , Watkins explains finding the final Clayface monster look, recruiting Paul for his cameo and creating Gotham City.

The Clayface name has been used by several villains in Batman comics. How did you land on the Matt Hagen version instead of the first iteration, Basil Karlo?

It was really landed by Mike Flanagan and the script. I read all of them, Basil Karlo and all, afterward because there are bits and bobs that are kind of cherry-picked from all over the place. But the key journey, and that’s what Mike had chosen, was the Matt Hagen version. If you’d have gone with Basil Karlo, it’s a little bit too gothic or too hard to do in such a modern idiom. The Matt Hagen is a more relatable version. Whether it’s Basil Karlo and Boris Karloff, there are all those characters that it’s referring back to in the Golden Age of Hollywood, that sort of thing. This is something that can sit in our contemporary time. Our Gotham is not entirely contemporary. It slightly steals from a few different genres. We wanted it to be slightly timeless, but it can play as contemporary.

This is the first time we’re seeing Gotham in the rebooted DC Universe. Did you have a specific year or time you wanted to set the world in?

We deliberately wanted it to be a bit muddy. James Price, our brilliant production designer, and I talked a lot about creating the sense of the world, and we wanted it to feel like a character in the movie. We wanted this oppressive world where the buildings really dominate. We looked at a lot of 1930s German expressionist cinema with huge dominant buildings and the odd angles and the noir-ish shadows. We also looked at street photography from New York from the ’70s, the ’80s and the ’90s. It was all before New York had been cleaned up. The lighting is different. It’s a lot of neon. There’s a lot of practical lighting. There’s a lot of dirt and eccentricity on the street. We wanted to definitely frame Gotham as a contrast to Coast City, with the colors, the bright sunshine, the sky, the sea. You see verdant greens and textures and stuff like that, which you don’t really see in Gotham. You barely see the sky, and it’s a very heavy atmosphere.

There are so many face-swapping scares in the movie. How many of them were practical camera tricks vs. special effects?

A lot of it is in camera. The scene in the nightclub where he comes in and he’s on this dark, lethal, vengeful journey, I wanted to give the audience permission to enjoy his payback before it goes too far. There’s a lot of in-camera wipes. We did so much stuff old-school. He takes somebody out, then he goes past a pillar, then I knew that I’d use that pillar as a wipe, then I do the scene again with another actor and they’d come out of the pillar or Tom would come out of the pillar. It was really good fun.

Did you have a contortionist for the nightclub scene too?

My guiding thing is if I can do it practically, I will try and do it practically. So after that fall down the stairs, which is a stunt with two stunt people, then they’re all on the floor, we were like, “Well, should we try it with a contortionist?” for that sense of bodies out of shape. If you can do it in camera, why not, right?

That sequence also has a quick cameo from Aaron Paul, who plays Matt’s dad in one of his transformations. How did you get him to shoot that scene?

It was like, “Who can we get to play Matt’s dad?” And I really, really love Aaron Paul as an actor. I know it’s tiny, but I think he was living in Paris, and so somebody said, “Why don’t we reach out?” He’s such a nice man, and he came in and was just a really good sport and a really fine actor. It’s a tiny moment, and it’s a sort of really an Easter egg, isn’t it? But the idea that Matt’s not his father and sort of thing. It was a pleasure to meet him. He was like, “Yeah, cool DC movie. I’ll show my face for a moment.” It was very nice of him.

How did you decide on the final look for the Clayface monster?

I took everything as a reference and tried to choose, because there are so many versions in the comics. We did about 19 different iterations. You want to honor the comics, but at the same time, you want to make sure it can work as live-action because it’s obviously a different medium. The key thing for me was making sure that it captured the emotion, the man inside the monster. I was particularly obsessed with his left eye and the pain and the heartbreak within that and the scream, the quality of his voice. I first responded in Mike’s script to the idea of the tragedy and the journey of his character and where he ends up and going with him.

It was an awful lot of work and tiny tweaks. Where one fold of flesh goes makes such a difference. It’s sort of unquantifiable, but you just have to look at it and something about that feels good and real. It was a lot of work, but it was fun.

How did you pull off the suffocation scene where Matt kills his friend, Corey, by pulling him into his body?

The actual pulling into the body is practical with augmentation, but he is wearing a rig on his body with a big cavity in it so he could pull Josh [James], who plays Corey, into his chest. It’s like his face in the airplane. That is prosthetic makeup, not VFX. There’s a tactile quality that just reads when it’s on camera, that I think is very hard to replicate.

So the airplane scene, where he has to cut the strips of clay between his eyes with scissors, is mostly practical?

He had contact lenses, and then he had prosthetic makeup on. He actually had five pairs of scissors. We had sharp ones, blunt ones, rubber ones, one with a green screen tip, one without a tip. It was all on a gimbal, so the bathroom could move in real time and create the jolts. I was on the microphone talking everyone through the scene and jolts and Tom’s reactions. Tom figured out a way to — it sounds awful — where he could shove it in slightly above his eye, but the way it reads on camera, you can’t tell. He was quite in control and safe. For the close-ups, we had an eyeball, which was enormous, with a massive pair of scissors.

How many different facial prosthetics did you have for Tom to wear?

We had so many stages. I can’t say how many prosthetics, but we had like 65 stages at one point. That was all with bandages and this and that, but there was an awful lot because there were subtle differences between different melts and droops, and some that can have a pulley that you could tug. Obviously, some of these things you can augment with VFX because Tom can’t literally do that. But always having that base layer again gives you something that has a sort of heft to it.

I kept looking for a bat flying around or some kind of reference to Batman, but there isn’t anything overt. Did you ever plan to include more Easter eggs in the movie?

I actually think there are lots of Easter eggs that I probably don’t even know about because the graphics department was always throwing in posters and stuff. What I really responded to was the fact that it was a standalone story, and so for me to read that and then to try and get too cute or crowbar something in that wasn’t merited to the narrative felt gimmicky, I suppose. There was zero pressure to do it. I signed up to a certain story, which I believed in, and I just tried to tell that to the best of my abilities.

After the movie ends, do you have any plan for where Clayface goes next? Is he getting ready to fight Robert Pattinson’s Batman or another DC hero?

That’s a question for James Gunn. I liked the standalone nature of it. I liked how it felt like it introduced a character. But I wasn’t trying to introduce the character to go, “OK, what next?” I was trying to introduce the character as a full meal in itself.

Un matin, sans crier gare, Inès Berdugo se réveille avec une drôle de pustule sur le menton. Rendez-vous chez le dermatologue peu concluants, crèmes, incantations… Rien ne se passe. Elle va finalement voir une spécialiste en décodage thérapeutique qui lui dit de but en blanc qu’elle n’a pas fait le deuil de son père. Décédé dix ans auparavant, alors qu’elle n’était qu’une adolescente, le fantôme de celui-ci revenait la hanter, en ressortant par tous ses pores. Inès n’avait-elle effectivement pas eu le temps de « faire son deuil » ? De ces questionnements, elle construit Du formol dans le cœur . Une série documentaire faite en cinq épisodes qui la suit dans son voyage autour de la mort, pour enfin réussir à désemplir son cœur.

Peux-tu te présenter et me raconter ton parcours ?

Inès Berdugo : J’ai commencé par des études en arts visuels à la Haute école d’art et de design de Genève, avec des intervenants vidéastes qui m’ont donné envie de faire des films. Puis je suis allée à la Cambre, à Bruxelles, faire un master de texte et création littéraire. Ça m’a beaucoup aidée pour l’écriture de films. J’ai ensuite réalisé ma première série documentaire sur le deuil, Du formol dans le cœur .

D’où part cette série ?

Mon père est décédé quand j’avais 15 ans, d’une rupture d’anévrisme. Dix ans plus tard, j’ai eu un énorme bouton sur le menton, qui ne faisait que grossir. Les médecins ne comprenaient pas d’où ça venait. Je suis allée voir une femme qui fait du décodage thérapeutique, recommandée par ma mère : elle m’a dit que le menton est associé au deuil, et les problèmes de peau à un conflit de séparation. N’ayant jamais vu mon père mort, je me suis dit qu’il fallait que j’aille voir la mort en vrai pour accepter qu’elle existe. La seule mort que j’avais vue avant, c’était celle de mon lapin. Aller voir des gens qui travaillent autour de la mort (croque-mort, thanatopractrice) et même une rabbine, m’a permis de comprendre comment je pouvais avancer sur ce chemin. Leur regard et leur expertise m’ont aidée à appréhender le deuil de manière plus douce. Il y a également ma famille, que je conçois comme des personnages « experts » à leur manière.

Et justement, comment ça s’est passé quand tu as inclus ta famille ?

On n’avait jamais vraiment parlé du deuil de mon père jusqu’à ce que la série serve de prétexte. J’ai pu échanger avec mon frère, ma sœur, ma mère, et j’ai réalisé que chacun avait vécu ce deuil différemment. Ma sœur, par exemple, semblait avoir « fait le tour » très rapidement. J’ai trouvé ça salvateur de pouvoir enfin mettre mes émotions en mots.

Tu es à la fois derrière et devant la caméra . Qu’est-ce que ce double rôle a produit ?

J’étais dans un endroit très intime avec mes protagonistes, donc il me semblait juste de me mettre moi-même dans une position vulnérable, de me donner à voir autant que les autres m’offraient leur intimité. C’est un regard engagé, qui ne les enferme pas dans un cadre. Me prendre comme personnage sert de fil rouge à cette quête. Ce qui m’intéressait le plus dans le processus, c’était la rencontre, l’échange, ce qui allait émaner de ça.

On sent chez toi une grande spontanéité face à un sujet lourd. Qu’est-ce que ça apporte d’aborder les choses de façon décomplexée ?

Ce qui m’intéresse, c’est de traiter des sujets douloureux avec humour. Mon court métrage Les golfes se creusent parle de la calvitie, qui est en soi une forme de perte, c’est douloureux et pas seulement pour les hommes, mais pour l’entourage qui vit par procuration cette « perte ». Mon dernier film, Les yeux brouillés , parle d’une phase de l’amour où on n’est plus en symbiose avec l’autre. La vie n’est faite que de micro-deuils : on dit au revoir à un travail, une ville, des gens. Et ce qui m’intéresse, c’est de savoir comment on continue à vivre quand quelque chose disparaît. Le sujet, c’est autant la vie que la mort. Je n’ai jamais cherché à alléger ce sujet en l’évitant, car c’est justement le fait de ne pas en parler, de le rendre tabou, qui rend les choses lourdes.

Tout part souvent d’un détail physique : un bouton, des cheveux, des larmes…

Complètement. J’ai besoin de choses concrètes, donc ça part toujours d’un détail du corps pour aller vers quelque chose de plus intérieur, que les personnages ne peuvent pas exprimer par les mots. C’est le contraste entre le « petit bobo » et toute la grande problématique intérieure qui se joue derrière. C’est là que le drame opère, et c’est là aussi que se loge la légèreté.

Vois-tu dans tes projets une forme de « sublimation » de la peine ?

Mon moteur, c’est la réparation plus que la sublimation. Il y a une envie de réparer quelque chose de douloureux, par l’humour ou la poésie. L’image permet de mettre en miroir, d’ouvrir une porte. En parler, décaler le sujet, l’emmener vers quelque chose d’un peu fantastique ou humoristique, ça aide dans ce processus de réparation.

Finalement, la pustule ayant disparu, cela veut-il dire que tu as « fait ton deuil » ?

Je pense que ce projet m’a permis d’accéder à un endroit plus concret de mon deuil. Il y a un avant et un après la série, car j’ai enfin accepté que ça dure toute la vie, qu’il n’y ait pas de fin à ce deuil. Je suis juste moins dans le déni, j’ai plus d’outils pour le comprendre. Même si la série suit un schéma en étapes, dans la réalité, le deuil est un mouvement circulaire, jamais vraiment terminé, toujours en construction.

article_text:
Che il videogioco abbia smesso da tempo di essere mero intrattenimento per trasformarsi in un fenomeno più ampio, una lente attraverso cui osservare alcune tendenze della società contemporanea, è ormai un dato di fatto. Che questo medium , poi, ben si fonda ed entri in un fertilo dialogo con l’arte contemporanea lo si è visto chiaramente negli ultimi anni: il dibattito critico — alimentato anche da figure di rilievo come Hans Ulrich Obrist nell’indagare la mutazione digitale delle istituzioni e delle pratiche espositive — riconosce nel motore grafico e nel codice binario un territorio d’elezione per le ultime tendenze visuali. Non si tratta più, infatti, soltanto di citare un’estetica pop o di recuperare la nostalgia dei cabinati, ma di fare i conti con un medium che ha ridefinito radicalmente i concetti di spazio, immersione, autorialità e corpo fisico: basti pensare alle manipolazioni minimali di Cory Arcangel sui vecchi flussi di codice, alle simulazioni architettoniche e distopiche di Lawrence Lek , o, ancora, alle vertiginose coreografie post-umane dell’artista cinese Lu Yang (di cui abbiamo parlato qui ): artisti, questi, che hanno dimostrato attraverso avatar, algoritmi e la tipica estetica del gaming come lo schermo si possa fare saggio visivo e critica sociale.

È all’interno di questo orizzonte teorico che si inserisce anche la mostra PLAYERS. Giochi, videogiochi, cultura e società , ospitata fino al 14 febbraio 2027 negli spazi del Museo M9 a Venezia Mestre . Curata da Fabio Viola con Michelangela Di Giacomo, Giuseppe Cosenza e Damiano Bordoni, l’esposizione sceglie di affrontare il fenomeno ludico non come una sequenza di cimeli tecnologici, ma come un immenso archivio di forme e comportamenti sociali, inserito in una direzione strategica fortemente voluta dal presidente della Fondazione di Venezia Vincenzo Marinese e dalla direttrice del museo Serena Bertolucci.

Il percorso espositivo, tradotto in forma concreta grazie al progetto allestitivo dell’architetto Valentina Babolin e del multimedia designer Vinicio Bordin, si articola in tre sezioni ben calibrate. La prima, #Play , ricostruisce la genealogia del medium dagli esperimenti accademici degli anni Cinquanta e Sessanta fino ai reperti pionieristici (tra cui esemplari storici come Computer Space , Pong e Dragon’s Lair ) e alle console che hanno abitato le camerette degli anni Novanta, fino alla postazione contemporanea.

La sezione #Watch sposta invece l’asse sul versante spettacolare e visivo, mettendo in cortocircuito il videogioco con il cinema, le trasmissioni eSport e la fotografia virtuale. Qui, pietre miliari di questo medium vengono osservate nella loro forza formale, dimostrando come l’esperienza della visione si sovrapponga a quella della fruizione artistica. Infine, #Create disinnesca il confine tra autore e fruitore: attraverso ecosistemi complessi, il pubblico diventa progettista di mondi, rispecchiando quell’idea di co-creazione che attraversa tutta la ricerca digitale contemporanea.

Ad arricchire l’impianto contribuiscono poi materiali inediti e le testimonianze video di maestri internazionali del calibro di Sid Meier, Yuka Kitamura e Jon Wilcox , accanto a un’attenta attenzione all’accessibilità, suggellata dall’uso pionieristico del dispositivo Jimmy per visitatori in sedia a rotelle.

article_text:
Après Faute d’amour (2017), qui sondait la déliquescence d’un couple à travers les yeux de son enfant, le cinéaste revient à ce modèle familial pour mieux le dévisager, le défigurer, le dé­construire. Parfaitement lisse, le trio formé par Gleb (Dmitri Mazourov), Galina (Iris Lebedeva) et leur fils unique adolescent apparaît déjà comme une utopie décharnée, isolée du monde et de ses vices.

Andreï Zviaguintsev : « L’enjeu principal, c’est celui du choix »

À ceci près que le couple se rend chaque jour en ville : Gleb pour se voir intimer d’envoyer ses salariés sur le front en Ukraine ; Galina pour rejoindre en secret l’homme qu’elle aime. Le cinéaste ne cherche pas à sauver moralement les apparences du masque social, autrement dit la vie de famille dans cette maison filmée comme un panoptique, où chacun des personnages se surveille et se contrôle. L’extérieur se lit alors comme l’envers du masque, le lieu d’une vérité inavouable à l’un et à l’autre et sans doute pour eux-mêmes.

À l’instar de Chabrol en son temps, Minotaure soulève une question glaçante : jusqu’où peut-on aller pour préserver le masque ? Jusqu’à quel degré d’aliénation ? Appliquée au contexte de la guerre en Ukraine, la réponse – tout aussi glaçante – n’en est que plus frontalement politique, car, enfin, Gleb fait partie des puissants de ce monde. Les pauvres, les chômeurs, les artistes, dont le « troisième homme » du récit en est une forme de synthèse, sont sacrifiés sur l’autel de l’indifférence. Un constat d’autant plus noir qu’il est filmé avec ce sens de la tragédie cher à Andreï Zviaguintsev, réduit à son essence muette : l’image d’un couple qui s’enlace dans l’obscurité, rien que l’obscurité.

Minotaure d’Andreï Zviaguintsev (Les Films du Losange, 2h15), sortie le 14 octobre

article_text:
Carmelo Bene in un museo. La bestemmia è già compiuta. Lui , che del teatro aveva fatto un attentato alla rappresentazione, consegnato alla fotografia. Lui, che aveva liquidato il personaggio, disertato l’interpretazione, mandato al diavolo la psicologia e i suoi rispettabili funzionari, finalmente fermo. Immobile. Catalogato. Una fotografia! Come conservare un terremoto in una scatola da scarpe. Eppure, proprio nell’insensatezza dell’operazione, si annida qualcosa di pertinente: quelle immagini non pretendono di restituire la scena, ma mostrano la concretezza di un’esperienza che aveva fatto dell’irripetibile la propria necessità.

Al MACRO di Roma , Una stanza per Bene. Tracce di quattro lavori di Carmelo Bene evita la consueta celebrazione del genio nazionale, possibilmente defunto e dunque finalmente innocuo. Il progetto si articola in quattro appuntamenti, dal novembre 2026 al marzo 2027, dedicati ad Addio porco , Caligola , Salomè e S.A.D.E. . La scelta di procedere per episodi sottrae l’artista alla tentazione antologica: nessuna biografia definitiva, nessuna illusione di possederne l’intera vicenda attraverso una visita.

Carmelo Bene al MACRO di Roma

I curatori Claudio Fazzini , Giuseppe Garrera e Federico Primosig appartengono a quella rara categoria di studiosi per i quali la conoscenza non coincide con l’amministrazione delle informazioni. Hanno inseguito materiali dispersi, interrogato fondi dimenticati, ricostruito provenienze e individuato fotografie originali talvolta conosciute soltanto attraverso riproduzioni digitali. Alcune sono riemerse persino fra i banchi di Porta Portese, dove un frammento della storia teatrale può tranquillamente trovarsi accanto a una cornice scompagnata. L’ironia è feroce: ciò che aveva scandalizzato una generazione torna alla luce grazie alla pazienza di chi riconosce quanto altri hanno smesso di guardare.

L’indagine assume così una dimensione archeologica. Non si cerca il capolavoro intatto, ma si ricostruiscono le condizioni della sua esistenza. Il culto dell’artista ha spesso prodotto l’effetto contrario alla conoscenza: una venerazione tanto assoluta da rendere superflua qualsiasi domanda. Tutto geniale, tutto irripetibile, tutto incomprensibile. Comodissimo. La grandezza, quando diventa dogma, dispensa persino dalla fatica di osservare.

Addio porco , rappresentato nel 1963 al Laboratorio di Piazza San Cosimato, riconduce a una stagione di sperimentazione particolarmente radicale. Il lavoro rielabora Gregorio, cabaret dell’800 , presentato al Ridotto del Teatro Eliseo nel 1961, esasperandone la struttura fino a trasformare la declamazione poetica in una catastrofe della parola. Quattro attori recitano versi ottocenteschi, cantano, gridano, si vestono, si svestono, si truccano. La recitazione procede verso un eccesso che non produce maggiore espressività, ma la sua dissoluzione. Le parole si deformano, la voce perde articolazione, il linguaggio precipita in suoni gutturali. Giovanni Calendoli, sulla Fiera Letteraria del novembre 1961, descriveva già nella precedente versione questa progressiva trasformazione degli attori in presenze incapaci di parlare. Non era il silenzio dopo la parola: era la parola che, consumata dalla propria ostentazione, diventava impossibile.

La seconda parte introduce un rovesciamento ancora più insolente. Dopo aver declamato, gli attori mangiano. Non fingono, non interpretano personaggi intenti a consumare un pasto. Mangiano realmente. Spaghetti, antipasti, portate servite in scena. Una tavola apparecchiata, una cucina improvvisata, il tempo ordinario della digestione che prende possesso del palcoscenico. Le cronache dell’epoca raccontano lo sconcerto degli spettatori, in attesa che qualcuno ricominciasse a recitare. Come se lo spettacolo si fosse interrotto per una pausa gastronomica. Non comprendevano che proprio quella sospensione costituiva l’atto teatrale più radicale.

La bocca, antico strumento della declamazione, diventava il luogo della sua destituzione. Prima pronunciava versi, poi produceva mugolii, infine masticava. L’apparato fonatorio si riconciliava brutalmente con quello digerente, ricordando che la poesia, prima di diventare patrimonio dello spirito, attraversa un organismo fatto di saliva e muscoli. Non era un semplice espediente scandalistico, ma un’aggressione alla rispettabilità della comunicazione. Il sublime della poesia ottocentesca finiva letteralmente fra i denti.

Le fotografie e le recensioni esposte permettono di osservare anche il disorientamento della critica davanti a qualcosa che sfuggiva alle categorie disponibili. Le testimonianze di Salvatore Vendittelli restituiscono la radicalità dell’esperimento, mentre gli articoli dell’epoca mostrano quanto fosse difficile distinguere la provocazione dall’elaborazione di un nuovo linguaggio scenico. La stessa esperienza del Laboratorio romano, segnata anche dallo scandalo di Cristo ’63 e dagli eccessi dell’artista argentino Alberto Greco, appartiene a una stagione nella quale la trasgressione non era ancora diventata un genere culturale da amministrare.

Gli appuntamenti successivi allargheranno l’indagine al Caligola di Camus, che aveva segnato l’esordio teatrale del regista, alla deformazione dell’universo decadente di Wilde in Salomè e ai dispositivi del potere affrontati in S.A.D.E. . Quattro territori di una medesima insubordinazione, senza la pretesa di ricondurli a un ordinato progresso stilistico.

L’allestimento possiede una sobrietà pertinente. Le fotografie, di dimensioni contenute, sono disposte su sottili mensole lignee; lunghi pannelli verticali riportano recensioni e ricostruzioni storiche. La relativa nudità dell’ambiente rinuncia alla tentazione di ricreare scenograficamente gli spettacoli. Il percorso richiede attenzione, ma sarebbe stato assai più discutibile trasformarlo in un’esperienza immersiva. Un artista così irriducibile trasformato in effetto speciale: un destino forse più crudele della dimenticanza.

Palestinian Sound Archive

Nella Sala Audio, il Palestinian Sound Archive , fondato da Mo’Min Swaitat e curato da Alice Labor , propone un’esperienza profondamente diversa. Cassette, vinili e registrazioni attraversano decenni di vita musicale palestinese, dalle tradizioni popolari al funk, dalla disco music alle sperimentazioni sonore. Attraverso Majazz Project emerge una Palestina che canta, balla, festeggia, si contraddice. Una società che esiste anche al di fuori della propria tragedia. È questo l’aspetto politicamente più significativo: sottrarre una cultura all’obbligo di essere raccontata esclusivamente attraverso la sofferenza. La presenza di generi internazionali accanto alle tradizioni locali contraddice inoltre l’immagine di un’identità immobile, rivelando contaminazioni, mode e sensibilità urbane. Perfino la spensieratezza, quando a un popolo viene negata la complessità della propria esistenza, può diventare una forma di resistenza.

La resistenza culturale nell’opera di Noor Abed

Nella Sala Video, we walk in our sleep المُتَجاوِزُون di Noor Abed , anch’esso curato da Alice Labor, sviluppa una riflessione affidata ai corpi. Girato in Palestina su pellicola Super 8, il film intreccia i monologhi di due donne a movimenti corali e gesti rituali. Il paesaggio non costituisce uno sfondo illustrativo, ma una presenza attraversata da relazioni, assenze e stratificazioni storiche. La coreografia non traduce una tesi politica in movimento: costruisce una conoscenza fisica, nella quale individuo e comunità si incontrano senza annullarsi. La grana della pellicola introduce una temporalità distante dall’immediatezza delle immagini contemporanee, chiedendo allo spettatore di osservare anziché consumare.

Sarebbe arbitrario stabilire una parentela estetica fra queste esperienze. Le condizioni storiche, le urgenze politiche e i procedimenti artistici divergono profondamente. Eppure, la loro contemporanea presenza al MACRO consente di attraversare linguaggi che rifiutano interpretazioni univoche. La fotografia trattiene un gesto senza poterlo ripetere, la musica racconta una società attraverso le sue trasformazioni, il cinema di Abed affida ai corpi ciò che le parole non esauriscono.

Resta quella stanza dedicata al grande irregolare del teatro italiano. Le fotografie sulle mensole, i ritagli di giornale, le voci di chi c’era. Un piccolo repertorio di oggetti sopravvissuti a uno spettacolo nel quale quattro attori, dopo aver massacrato la poesia ottocentesca, si sedevano a mangiare. Gli spettatori aspettavano che il teatro ricominciasse. Sessant’anni dopo, siamo ancora qui, davanti alle fotografie, ad aspettare che qualcuno ci dica quando sia finito.

article_text:
アメリカ・マイアミの体験型アートセンター「Superblue」の初となる海外拠点「スーパーブルー 京都（Superblue Kyoto）」が、2027年初頭に京都駅東南部エリアにオープン。オープニング展として、ジェームズ・タレルの大規模展が開催される。

2020年の設立以来、体験型アートを専門とする現代アーティストの活動を支援するとともに、芸術と身体的な体験が交差する領域で生まれる作品の制作・発表の場を提供してきたSuperblue。2021年、マイアミに初となるアートセンターを開館し、エス・デヴリン、チームラボ、ジェームズ・タレルによる大規模な作品を展示した。

このたび開業する初の海外拠点「スーパーブルー 京都」は、2025年に開業した 「チームラボ バイオヴォルテックス 京都 - 大成建設」 の向かいに立地。両施設は、京都市が推進する「京都駅東南部エリア活性化方針」のもと、同エリアの市有地に「新たな価値を生み出す創造・発信拠点」となる施設を設置・運営する事業の一環となる。

オープニングを飾るのは、ジェームズ・タレルの長期展覧会。1960年代の初期作品から最新作まで、タレルが半世紀以上にわたって探究してきた光と空間、人間の知覚をテーマとする作品群が展示される。果てしなく広がる色彩の空間に身を委ねる体験や、光がもたらす「かたち」と「奥行き」の交錯に目を凝らす体験など、普段意識しない光の存在を認識させるインスタレーションを通じて、世界のとらえ方を問い直す体験をもたらすという。

展示作品やオープン日、チケット情報などの詳細は、2026年12月頃に発表予定。

article_text:
The new John H. McCall Theater, a third screen at the Austin Film Society ‘s AFS Cinema, will open its doors on October 24, kicking off a weekend-long event that will bring James Gray ‘s crime thriller “ Paper Tiger ” to the Texas venue. IndieWire shares the exclusive details below.

Martin Scorsese’s “ The Color of Money ” (1986), Sofia Coppola’s “ Marie Antoinette ” (2006), and the 1995 fashion documentary “Unzipped” will also screen in new 4K restorations through the theater’s first weekend. On October 27, the theater will host a premiere of Neon’s “ Paper Tiger ,” along with a discussion between writer/director Gray and AFS founder and artistic director Richard Linklater .

“The McCall Theater will allow us to expand our programming and better serve the filmmakers, festivals, and audiences who have made the theater their home,” said Linklater. “It’s another step in the same journey we began four decades ago: creating a place where great films are discovered, filmmakers are supported, and a community gathers around the shared experience of cinema.”

The McCall will seat 169 people and feature 4K digital laser projection and 7.1 surround sound. AFS credits the additional third screen to a donation by Amy McCall, the wife of the late John McCall, who died in 2021. The McCalls had previously gifted a donation to AFS in 2016 that provided funds for the organization to renovate and reopen the shuttered Marchesa Theater as AFS Cinema. Celebrated by AFS as a decades-long supporter of the Texas film industry, John McCall was inducted into its Texas Film Hall of Fame in 2018.

AFS was first founded in 1985 by a then-twentysomething Linklater. The organization opened the repertory and first-run arthouse AFS Cinema in 2017, giving it its first permanent screening home. The venue had featured two screens and an event space until the addition of the McCall. Along with AFS Cinema, the organization also operates Austin Studios, a 20-acre facility for local productions, as well as Austin Public, a space for media professionals to train and collaborate.

“Paper Tiger” opens in theaters for the rest of the country starting November 13.

article_text:
Netflix’s push to release more films on the big screen hasn’t come without a few hiccups. Most recently, theater chains including Regal Cinemas are declining to play the streaming platform’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” on their Imax screens. Cinemark also turned down the “Cliff Booth” booking, according to sources.

“Cliff Booth,” which stars Brad Pitt and is directed by David Fincher, is still set to play on AMC’s Imax screens for a two-week release beginning Nov. 25 before releasing on the streaming platform Dec. 23.

News of the release plans was first reported by Puck .

Lionsgate’s “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” is currently set to occupy a majority of cinemas with its upcoming Nov. 20 premiere. The exhibitors would have had to give up some of their “Hunger Games” Imax screens for “Cliff Booth,” which streams just a month later — a no-go for some circuits.

With AMC’s 200 Imax screens available in the U.S. and several others offered internationally by independent cinemas, “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” will play on more than 500 screens worldwide. Regal has approximately 100 Imax screens and Cinemark around 20, while some other smaller chains will reportedly not book “Cliff Booth” either.

Fincher’s film is one of several upcoming Netflix titles slated for a theatrical release, including “Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew,” which will see a wide release (including Imax screens) for almost 50 days, “The Mosquito Bowl,” “Ray Gunn” and “Charlie vs. the Chocolate Factory.” The streaming platform reported grosses for the first time for the big-screen debut earlier this month of “La Bola Negra,” which brought in over $277,000 across just four theaters and marked the second-highest screen average for a non-English language film behind 2019’s “Parasite.”
